paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. Paul doesn't open this letter with a to-do list. He opens with thanks, because he's heard about their faith in Christ Jesus and their love for all the saints (Colossians 1:3-4). And that faith and love come from a hope stored up in heaven (Colossians 1:5), so it's not something the Colossians had to cook up on their own.

Then look at what Paul asks for. He and Timothy haven't stopped praying that God would fill them with the knowledge of His will, so that they may walk in a manner worthy of the Lord, bearing fruit in every good work and growing in the knowledge of God (Colossians 1:9-10). Baker, knowing God's will is for WALKING, not just for knowing! And the strength for that walk comes from God, who strengthens them with all power for full endurance and patience (Colossians 1:11). I need a sit-down after one tray, so I'm glad the power isn't mine.

And here's why they can do it with joy. The Father has rescued us from the dominion of darkness and brought us into the kingdom of His beloved Son, in whom we have redemption, the forgiveness of sins (Colossians 1:13-14). I know a little something about being pulled out of the dark, friend, and I'm still not over it. You don't grow in the Word to earn your place. You grow because the place is already yours, and that's the best reason to keep baking.
